abstract: Measurements of inclusive jet suppression in heavy ion collisions at the LHC provide direct sensitivity to the physics of jet quenching. In a sample of lead-lead collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76 TeV corresponding to an integrated luminosity of approximately 7 inverse microbarns, ATLAS has measured jets with a calorimeter over the pseudorapidity interval |$\eta$| < 2.1 and over the transverse momentum range 38 < pT < 210 GeV. Jets were reconstructed using the anti-$k_t$ algorithm with values for the distance parameter that determines the nominal jet radius of R = 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5. The centrality dependence of the jet yield is characterized by the jet "central-to-peripheral ratio," $R_{cp}$. Jet production is found to be suppressed by approximately a factor of two in the 10% most central collisions relative to peripheral collisions. $R_{cp}$ varies smoothly with centrality as characterized by the number of participating nucleons. The observed suppression is only weakly dependent on jet radius and transverse momentum. These results provide the first direct measurement of inclusive jet suppression in heavy ion collisions and complement previous measurements of dijet transverse energy imbalance at the LHC.

data_abstract: CERN-LHC. Measurements of the ratio, Rcp, between jet production in the central to peripheral regions in   Lead Lead collisions at a centre of mass energy/nucleon  of 2.76 TeV.  Jets are reconstructed with |eta|<2.1,  covering the jet PT range 38-210 GeV, using the   anti-Kt algorithm with norminal jet radii of R=0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5.  Seven regions of centrality are considered from   the most peripheral of 60-80% to the most central 0-10%. Rcp is studied as a function of jet PT, number of participating  nucleons NPART and R for each of the centrality regions, as well as the ratio of Rcp/Rcp(R=0.2) as a function of jet PT  for each R=0.3, 0.4 and 0.5.    Finally values of the covariance matrix for staistical correlations between jet PT bins are given.  In the tables the  first systematic errors are from JES, JER, efficiency, xin and Rcoll and are 100% correlated in PT.  The second  systematic errors are those that are partially correlated or uncorrelated in pt, taken to be 100% uncorrelated,  from the regularization parameter.
